about: Invented notes and stories for the A4 matcher (25 Nov 2026). Every note, name and story here was made up for this file: none comes from a real account or a real child. note: one entry per note unit (a line, or a sentence of a longer line), joined by joiner. paras: the observation part, one array per paragraph, each sentence [text, gold]. gold: '1' or '1,3' = backed by those note units; 'x' = says something the note does not show; 'r' = the educator's reading with no source; 'r:2' = reading that points at unit 2. Labelled by hand before lib/source-lines.ts existed. Split: odd positions tune, even positions held out.

note: Aria at the playdough table rolling long snakes
cut them into pieces with the plastic knife and counted them 1 2 3 4 5
said "I made five sausages for the barbecue"
gave one to Leo and one to me
stories.title: Five sausages for the barbecue
paras: Aria spent time at the playdough table rolling long snakes of dough.
She used the plastic knife to cut them into pieces.
Then she counted the pieces out loud, one to five.
Aria told us, "I made five sausages for the barbecue".
She shared them, giving one to Leo and one to her teacher.
This was a lovely moment of kindness and turn-taking.
r
stories.reading: Aria was using counting in her play and linking it to something she knows from home.
stories.next: We will add tongs and paper plates to the playdough table.

note: Mateo built a ramp with the long wooden block and a crate.
Rolled cars down it, the red one went furthest.
He moved the crate higher and tried again.
Called out "faster now!"
stories.title: How high can the ramp go?
paras: Mateo made a ramp by leaning the long wooden block against a crate.
He rolled cars down the ramp and watched where each one stopped.
The red car travelled the furthest.
Next Mateo lifted the crate higher and tested the ramp again.
"Faster now!" he called out.
He measured each car's distance with a metre ruler.
x
stories.reading: Mateo was testing a theory about height and speed.
stories.next: We will offer different surfaces for the ramp.

note: Isla painting at the easel, only blue and yellow
mixed them on the paper and it went green
she gasped and said "green came!"
painted the whole page green then wanted to hang it up
stories.title: Green came!
paras: Isla chose blue and yellow paint at the easel.
As she mixed the two colours on her paper, they turned green.
Isla gasped and said, "green came!"
She kept going until the whole page was green.
When she finished she asked to hang her painting up.
Isla was discovering how colours change when they meet.
stories.reading: Isla noticed a change she caused herself.
stories.next: We will put out red and white so she can try more mixing.

note: Noah at the sandpit digging a hole with the big spade
found a worm, held it in his palm
asked where it lives
we looked in the book about minibeasts together
stories.title: Noah's worm
paras: Noah dug a deep hole in the sandpit with the big spade.
He found a worm and gently held it in his open palm.
Noah wanted to know where the worm lives.
Together we looked through the minibeasts book to find out.
Noah then dug a new home for the worm under the tree.
x
He showed great care and curiosity for living things.
stories.reading: Noah is curious about the natural world.
stories.next: We will set up a worm farm.

note: Wiremu on the climbing frame, went up the net for the first time.
Stopped halfway, looked down, said "I'm scared".
I said take your time, he kept going.
At the top he waved to his friends.
stories.title: To the top of the net
paras: Today Wiremu climbed the net on the climbing frame for the very first time.
Halfway up he stopped and looked down.
He said, "I'm scared".
I told him to take his time, and he kept climbing.
When he reached the top he waved to his friends.
His friends cheered and clapped for him.
x
Wiremu showed courage in pushing through his fear.
r
stories.reading: Wiremu was taking a risk and managing it.
stories.next: We will keep the net available and encourage him to try the rope ladder.

note: Ruby in home corner, feeding the dolls
put a bib on baby and used a spoon
sang twinkle twinkle to put her to sleep
covered her with a blanket and whispered shh
stories.title: Ruby cares for baby
paras: Ruby played in the home corner, feeding the dolls.
She put a bib on the baby and fed her with a spoon.
Then she sang Twinkle Twinkle to help the baby fall asleep.
Ruby covered her with a blanket and whispered, "shh".
Ruby was showing what she knows about caring for others.
r
stories.reading: Ruby re-created routines from her own life.
stories.next: We will add a doll bath and towels.

note: Kai and Sam with the hose in the garden
Kai filled the watering can and watered the bean plants
noticed the beans had flowers, pointed and said "look, pink!"
counted the flowers, got to 8
stories.title: Pink flowers on the beans
paras: Kai was in the garden with Sam and the hose.
He filled up the watering can and gave the bean plants a drink.
Kai spotted flowers on the beans and pointed.
"Look, pink!" he said.
He counted the flowers carefully and got to eight.
Kai then picked a bean and tasted it.
x
stories.reading: Kai is noticing how plants grow and change.
stories.next: We will look for beans together next week.

note: Olivia doing a 24 piece puzzle of a farm.
Did the edges first, all by herself.
Got stuck on the sky pieces, tried turning them around.
Asked Mia to help and they finished it together.
stories.title: The farm puzzle
paras: Olivia chose a 24 piece farm puzzle.
She did all the edge pieces first, on her own.
The sky pieces were tricky, so she turned them around to see where they might fit.
Olivia asked Mia for help.
Together the two girls finished the puzzle.
She was using problem-solving strategies and knew when to ask for help.
stories.reading: Olivia persisted with a hard task.
stories.next: We will offer a 35 piece puzzle.

note: Hemi at mat time joined in the waiata
did all the actions for Tutira mai
afterwards asked to sing it again
taught Ella the actions
stories.title: Hemi leads the waiata
paras: At mat time Hemi joined in with our waiata.
He did every action for Tutira mai.
When it ended he asked if we could sing it again.
Later Hemi taught Ella how to do the actions.
He spoke to her in te reo Māori as he showed her.
x
stories.reading: Hemi is growing his confidence with te reo and waiata.
stories.next: We will invite Hemi to lead the waiata at mat time.

note: Zoe at the writing table drew a card for her nana
drew a heart and a sun
wrote Z and O and said that's my name
asked for an envelope
stories.title: A card for Nana
paras: Zoe sat at the writing table and made a card for her nana.
She drew a heart and a sun on the front.
Zoe wrote the letters Z and O and told us, "that's my name".
Then she asked for an envelope.
She is beginning to understand that writing carries a message.
stories.reading: Zoe is using marks and letters with purpose.
stories.next: We will add envelopes and stamps to the writing table.

note: Tama in the block corner building a tall tower.
It fell down twice, he laughed and started again.
Third time he put the big blocks at the bottom.
It stayed up and he said "strong one".
stories.title: A strong one
paras: Tama built a tall tower in the block corner.
It fell down twice.
Each time Tama laughed and started again.
On his third try he placed the big blocks at the bottom.
This time the tower stayed up.
"Strong one," Tama said.
He then added a flag on the top made from paper.
x
stories.reading: Tama was working out how to make a structure stable.
stories.next: We will offer photos of tall buildings.

note: Charlotte at lunch opened her own lunchbox and yoghurt
peeled her mandarin and shared pieces with Ava
put her rubbish in the bin without being asked
stories.title: Charlotte does it herself
paras: At lunchtime Charlotte opened her lunchbox and her yoghurt by herself.
She peeled her mandarin and shared some pieces with Ava.
When she finished she put her rubbish in the bin without being asked.
Charlotte is becoming more independent in her self-care.
r
stories.reading: Charlotte manages routines with confidence.
stories.next: We will invite Charlotte to help set the table.

note: Nikau found a snail on the path after rain
watched it move very slowly
said "it has a house on its back"
put a leaf in front of it to see if it would eat
stories.title: A house on its back
paras: After the rain Nikau found a snail on the path.
He crouched down and watched it slowly move along.
"It has a house on its back," he said.
Nikau put a leaf in front of the snail to see if it would eat it.
The snail ate a small hole in the leaf.
x
Nikau was forming his own theories about the snail.
stories.reading: Nikau is curious and asks his own questions.
stories.next: We will make a snail home with Nikau.

note: Harper at the light table with coloured shapes.
Made a pattern red blue red blue.
Said "it goes again and again".
Then made a house with a triangle roof.
stories.title: Again and again
paras: Harper explored the coloured shapes at the light table.
She made a repeating pattern of red, blue, red, blue.
"It goes again and again," Harper explained.
Next she used the shapes to build a house with a triangle roof.
Harper is noticing and making patterns.
stories.reading: Harper is showing early algebraic thinking through pattern.
stories.next: We will offer three-colour patterns.

note: Manaia at the carpentry table with Jess
hammered three nails into the wood
held the hammer near the end like I showed him
said "I'm making a boat for my dad"
stories.title: A boat for Dad
paras: Manaia worked at the carpentry table alongside Jess.
He hammered three nails into a piece of wood.
Manaia held the hammer near the end, the way he had been shown.
"I'm making a boat for my dad," he told me.
He painted the boat blue and took it home.
x
Manaia was using tools with skill and care.
stories.reading: Manaia is building confidence with real tools.
stories.next: We will add a saw for Manaia to try with support.

note: Lily at group time with the felt board story
put the three bears on the board in order big middle small
said the words with me "who's been eating my porridge"
wanted to be Goldilocks next time
stories.title: Who's been eating my porridge?
paras: At group time Lily joined in with the felt board story.
She placed the three bears on the board in order: big, middle and small.
Lily said the words along with me, "who's been eating my porridge".
She asked to be Goldilocks next time.
Lily also retold the whole story to her friends at lunch.
x
stories.reading: Lily is building her knowledge of story structure and size order.
stories.next: We will act out the story with costumes.

note: Ari arrived upset, held onto mum.
We read his favourite truck book together on the couch.
He calmed down and waved bye to mum at the window.
Then went straight to the trucks in the sandpit.
stories.title: Ari settles in
paras: Ari was upset when he arrived and held on tight to his mum.
We sat on the couch and read his favourite truck book together.
Ari calmed and waved goodbye to his mum from the window.
Then he went straight to play with the trucks in the sandpit.
Ari is learning that he can feel safe here.
r
stories.reading: A familiar book helped Ari manage the goodbye.
stories.next: We will keep the truck book by the door for mornings.

note: Grace on the bikes, rode the trike around the track
stopped at the stop sign every time
let Max go first at the bridge
said "you go, then me"
stories.title: You go, then me
paras: Grace rode the trike around the bike track.
She stopped at the stop sign every time she came to it.
At the bridge she let Max go first.
"You go, then me," said Grace.
Grace is learning about rules and taking turns.
She also helped Max when his bike got stuck in the grass.
x
stories.reading: Grace understands the rules of the track.
stories.next: We will add road signs she can set out herself.

note: Tane at the water trough with jugs and funnels
poured from the big jug into the small jug, it overflowed
said "too much!" and laughed
tried the funnel and poured slower
stories.title: Too much!
paras: Tane played at the water trough with the jugs and funnels.
He poured water from the big jug into the small jug until it overflowed.
"Too much!" Tane laughed.
Then he tried using the funnel and poured more slowly.
Tane was exploring capacity in a hands-on way.
stories.reading: Tane is learning about full, empty and too much.
stories.next: We will add measuring cups.

note: Ella and Sophie in the dress ups being doctors.
Ella put the stethoscope on Sophie's tummy.
Said "you need medicine, two spoons".
Wrote a prescription with squiggles.
stories.title: Doctor Ella
paras: Ella and Sophie played doctors in the dress up corner.
Ella listened to Sophie's tummy with the stethoscope.
"You need medicine, two spoons," she said.
Ella wrote Sophie a prescription with squiggles.
Then she gave her a pretend injection and a sticker for being brave.
x
Ella used her knowledge of the world in her play.
r
stories.reading: Ella is using writing for a purpose in her play.
stories.next: We will set up a doctor's clinic with appointment cards.

note: Rawiri helped make bread with Kaye
measured flour with the cup, 3 cups
kneaded the dough and said it feels sticky
waited at the oven window
stories.title: Making bread
paras: Rawiri helped Kaye make bread.
He measured three cups of flour with the cup.
As he kneaded the dough he told us it felt sticky.
Rawiri waited by the oven window to watch it bake.
He was so proud when he ate his own bread at afternoon tea.
x
stories.reading: Rawiri is learning about measurement through cooking.
stories.next: We will make pizza dough next week.

note: Mia on the swing, asked for a push
then tried to pump her legs by herself
said "look I'm doing it"
swung for a long time
stories.title: Look, I'm doing it
paras: Mia asked for a push on the swing.
Then she tried to pump her legs by herself.
"Look, I'm doing it," Mia called.
She kept swinging for a long time.
Mia was building strength and coordination.
r
stories.reading: Mia showed persistence in learning a new skill.
stories.next: We will encourage Mia to show a friend how to pump.

note: Finn with the magnifying glass looking at leaves.
Said the lines on the leaf look like roads.
Collected 5 different leaves in a basket.
Sorted them big to small on the mat.
stories.title: Roads on a leaf
paras: Finn used the magnifying glass to look closely at leaves.
He told me the lines on the leaf looked like roads.
Finn collected five different leaves in a basket.
He sorted them on the mat from biggest to smallest.
Finn then drew the leaves in his book with the lines on them.
x
Finn was making connections between nature and his own world.
stories.reading: Finn is a careful observer.
stories.next: We will make leaf rubbings together.

note: Sienna in the music area with the drums
played loud then soft when I said quiet mouse
copied my rhythm clap clap tap
made up her own song about her dog Biscuit
stories.title: A song for Biscuit
paras: Sienna explored the drums in the music area.
She played loudly, then softly when I said "quiet mouse".
Sienna copied my rhythm of clap, clap, tap.
She made up her own song about her dog, Biscuit.
Sienna is developing her musical skills.
r
stories.reading: Sienna listens and responds to sound.
stories.next: We will record Sienna's song.

note: Ihaia made a hut with sheets over the table
invited Rua and Pita inside
they took books in and torches
said "no grown ups allowed" laughing
stories.title: No grown-ups allowed
paras: Ihaia built a hut by draping sheets over the table.
He invited Rua and Pita to come inside.
The boys took books and torches in with them.
"No grown-ups allowed," Ihaia laughed.
Inside the hut the boys read stories to each other in the dark.
x
Ihaia was leading his friends in play.
stories.reading: Ihaia is building friendships.
stories.next: We will leave sheets out for building.

note: Jack at the train set joining tracks.
Made a big loop and a bridge.
When the train came off he fixed the gap.
Said "now it goes all the way round".
stories.title: All the way round
paras: Jack joined the train tracks together.
He made a big loop with a bridge.
When the train came off the track, Jack found the gap and fixed it.
"Now it goes all the way round," he said.
Jack was solving problems as they came up.
stories.reading: Jack is persistent and logical.
stories.next: We will add a second train so two can play.

note: Anahera at the collage table glued feathers and shells onto card
said it was a bird nest
asked for more glue, used a lot
showed her dad at pick up
stories.title: A bird nest
paras: Anahera glued feathers and shells onto card at the collage table.
She told us it was a bird nest.
Anahera asked for more glue and used plenty of it.
At pick up she proudly showed her dad.
Her dad hung it on their fridge at home.
x
stories.reading: Anahera is expressing her ideas through art.
stories.next: We will go looking for real nests.

note: Oscar fell off the balance beam, grazed knee
cried, came to me for a cuddle
said he wanted a bandaid with a dinosaur
went back and walked the beam again slowly
stories.title: Back on the beam
paras: Oscar fell off the balance beam and grazed his knee.
He cried and came to me for a cuddle.
Oscar asked for a dinosaur bandaid.
Then he went back and walked along the beam again, slowly this time.
Oscar showed real resilience.
r
stories.reading: Oscar knows who to go to when he is hurt.
stories.next: We will practise on a lower beam.

note: Maia sorting the buttons into the muffin tin by colour.
Put all the red together then the blue.
Found one with two colours and said "it can go in both".
Counted the yellow ones, 7.
stories.title: It can go in both
paras: Maia sorted buttons by colour into the muffin tin.
She put all the red buttons together, then the blue.
Maia found a button with two colours.
"It can go in both," she said.
She counted seven yellow buttons.
Maia then made a necklace with the buttons on string.
x
Maia was thinking about how things can belong to more than one group.
stories.reading: Maia is classifying and reasoning.
stories.next: We will sort by size as well as colour.

note: Henry at the art table cutting paper with scissors
held them the right way up, thumb on top
cut along the line on the strip
made a fringe and stuck it on a crown
stories.title: Henry's crown
paras: Henry used the scissors at the art table to cut paper.
He held them correctly, with his thumb on top.
Henry cut along the line on a paper strip.
He made a fringe and stuck it onto a crown.
Henry wore his crown all afternoon and called himself the king.
x
stories.reading: Henry's fine motor skills are growing.
stories.next: We will offer curved lines to cut.

note: Aroha with the rākau sticks at mat time
tapped them together in time with the beat
passed the sticks to the next person in the circle
said "ka pai" to Wiremu when he did it
stories.title: Ka pai, Wiremu
paras: Aroha joined in with the rākau at mat time.
She tapped the sticks together in time with the beat.
Aroha passed the sticks on to the next person in the circle.
When Wiremu had his turn she told him, "ka pai".
Aroha is showing manaakitanga towards her friends.
stories.reading: Aroha is growing her sense of rhythm.
stories.next: We will learn a new rākau game.

note: William at the drawing table drew his family.
Mum, dad, baby and our dog.
Told me the baby is called Rosie and she cries a lot.
Gave the drawing to his mum.
stories.title: William's family
paras: William drew a picture of his family at the drawing table.
He drew his mum, his dad, the baby and the dog.
William told me the baby is called Rosie and that she cries a lot.
He gave his drawing to his mum.
His mum said she would frame it.
x
William is proud of his family and wanted to share about them.
r
stories.reading: William is talking about the people who matter to him.
stories.next: We will make a family wall with photos.

note: Pania kicking the ball with Hugo on the field
kicked it into the goal and jumped up and down
Hugo said my turn and she gave him the ball
they took turns for about 10 minutes
stories.title: Goal!
paras: Pania played ball with Hugo on the field.
She kicked the ball into the goal and jumped up and down.
When Hugo asked for a turn, Pania gave him the ball.
They took turns for around ten minutes.
Pania was learning to share and take turns.
stories.reading: Pania is building friendships through games.
stories.next: We will set up a small team game.

note: Archie at the science table with magnets
found that the magnet picked up the paperclips but not the pencil
said "it only likes metal"
tested the table leg and the door handle
stories.title: It only likes metal
paras: Archie explored magnets at the science table.
He found the magnet picked up paperclips but not a pencil.
"It only likes metal," Archie said.
He went on to test the table leg and the door handle.
The magnet stuck to the fridge in the kitchen too.
x
Archie was testing his theory.
stories.reading: Archie is using a scientific approach.
stories.next: We will make a magnet treasure hunt.

note: Kiri helped feed the chickens with me.
Threw the grain and counted the chickens, 4.
Found an egg in the nesting box, still warm.
Carried it inside very carefully with two hands.
stories.title: A warm egg
paras: Kiri helped me feed the chickens.
She threw the grain and counted four chickens.
In the nesting box Kiri found an egg that was still warm.
She carried it inside very carefully, using both hands.
Kiri was showing respect and care for our animals.
r
stories.reading: Kiri takes responsibility for living things.
stories.next: We will make a chicken roster.

note: Lucas in the sandpit making a road for the diggers
flattened the sand with his hand
made a tunnel and drove the digger through
the tunnel fell in, he said "oh no, roadworks"
stories.title: Roadworks
paras: Lucas made a road for the diggers in the sandpit.
He flattened the sand with his hand.
He made a tunnel and drove the digger through it.
When the tunnel fell in, Lucas said, "oh no, roadworks".
He called Noah over to help him rebuild it.
x
stories.reading: Lucas is bringing his knowledge of the world into play.
stories.next: We will add road cones and signs.

note: Ana reading the book Where is the Green Sheep with Pita
pointed at each sheep and said its colour
turned the pages herself
at the end said "there he is!"
stories.title: There he is!
paras: Ana and Pita read Where is the Green Sheep together.
She pointed at each sheep and named its colour.
Ana turned the pages herself.
At the end she said, "there he is!"
Ana is learning to love books.
r
stories.reading: Ana is enjoying sharing books with friends.
stories.next: We will read more books by the same author.

note: Leo at the obstacle course, crawled through the tunnel.
Jumped off the box with two feet.
Walked along the plank with arms out.
Did the whole course three times.
stories.title: Three times round
paras: Leo crawled through the tunnel on the obstacle course.
He jumped off the box landing on two feet.
Leo walked along the plank with his arms out for balance.
He went round the whole course three times.
On the last turn he timed himself with the sand timer.
x
Leo was building his gross motor skills.
r
stories.reading: Leo enjoys physical challenge.
stories.next: We will add a hopping section.

note: Moana watering the seedlings in the planter box
noticed one had two leaves now
asked "is it a baby tree?"
we said it was a sunflower and it will grow very tall
stories.title: Is it a baby tree?
paras: Moana watered the seedlings in the planter box.
She noticed one now had two leaves.
"Is it a baby tree?" she asked.
We told her it was a sunflower and would grow very tall.
Moana measured herself against the sunflower to compare.
x
stories.reading: Moana is noticing growth.
stories.next: We will measure the sunflower each week.

note: Thomas got upset when Jack took his car
yelled "mine!" and grabbed it back
I helped him use words, he said "I'm still using it"
Jack gave it back and they played side by side
stories.title: I'm still using it
paras: Thomas got upset when Jack took the car he was using.
He yelled, "mine!" and grabbed it back.
With support, Thomas used his words: "I'm still using it".
Jack gave the car back, and the two boys played side by side.
Thomas is learning to use words to solve problems.
stories.reading: Thomas is learning to manage big feelings.
stories.next: We will practise these words at group time.
